caption: Also accepts a single list argument
A single argument is returned unchanged

wolfram.note: A complex operand has no order, so both leave the call unevaluated (Max::nord in Wolfram); Wolfram keeps the arguments as written, Max[I, 3/2], where ours sorts them, Max(3/2, i).
sage.note: A complex operand has no order. Sage's max compares I with 3/2 through a symbolic relation and returns 3/2; ours leaves Max(3/2, i) unevaluated, as compute-engine and Wolfram do.
sympy.note: A complex operand has no order: SymPy's Max raises ('I' is not comparable), and ours leaves Max(3/2, i) unevaluated.
julia.note: Max is real-valued in Julia's mapping (Nemo's ball floor and ordering are real only); compute-engine's also takes a complex argument.
rust.note: std's sqrt is real-only: past the real domain it gives NaN, which the lane reports as an error and never as agreement; compute-engine continues to the principal complex value.

caption: Nested lists are flattened into the pool
The numeric arguments collapse to their maximum; symbolic ones stay
The max of two [[Interval]]s is the interval of possible maxima, $[1, 5]$
wolfram.note: Ours defines Max of Intervals as interval-valued (the interval of possible maxima, [1,5]); Wolfram's Max on Interval args collapses to a plain number (5), a different definition of the operation.
sympy.note: SymPy leaves Max(...) over an AccumBounds unevaluated; ours computes the image.

caption: A [[Finset]] has a largest member: the subset $\{1,3,4\}$ of $\{1,\dots,6\}$
The day's high from a handful of hourly readings. See [[Min]]
Multiple list arguments are flattened into one pool rather than compared pairwise
rust.note: The mapping takes two scalars; compute-engine's Max is variadic and flattens its list operands.

caption: With no arguments, compute-engine returns NaN rather than $-\infty$, the true identity element
wolfram.note: Max of nothing is NaN here; Wolfram returns the identity element -Infinity.
sage.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers "NaN" and Sage raises an error.
sympy.note: The maximum of nothing: SymPy answers −∞, compute-engine NaN.
julia.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers NaN, Julia raises an error (ArgumentError: reducing over an empty co).

caption: NaN poisons the result, overriding every other argument
sympy.note: Ours lets NaN poison the Max; SymPy's Max raises that nan is not comparable.
julia.note: The mapping compares with >, which treats a NaN operand as unordered and passes over it, where compute-engine's extremum is poisoned by NaN.

caption: The max of an empty list is NaN too
wolfram.note: compute-engine rules Max of an empty collection NaN (ERROR-MODEL §1: aggregates are NaN on empty input; the changelog drops the old -Infinity); Wolfram defines Max[{}] as -Infinity, the identity element for Max.
sage.note: Both decline on an empty collection: compute-engine answers NaN for Max([]), and Sage's max() raises ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty.
sympy.note: compute-engine rules Max of an empty collection NaN (ERROR-MODEL §1: aggregates are NaN on empty input); SymPy's Max() is the identity -∞.
julia.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers NaN, Julia raises an error (ArgumentError: reducing over an empty co).

caption: ComplexInfinity is unordered, so Max cannot compare it: the call stays unevaluated, as in Wolfram
sage.note: Sage orders unsigned infinity against 1 and answers ComplexInfinity; Wolfram and compute-engine leave Max(~oo, 1) unevaluated, and SymPy raises, since ~oo is not comparable.
sympy.note: compute-engine leaves the call unevaluated; SymPy raises, since zoo is not comparable.

caption: The empty [[Finset]] answers as an empty list does: NaN
wolfram.note: compute-engine rules Max of an empty collection NaN (ERROR-MODEL §1: aggregates are NaN on empty input); Wolfram defines Max[{}] as -Infinity.
sage.note: Python's max of an empty list raises; compute-engine answers NaN.
sympy.note: compute-engine rules Max of an empty collection NaN (ERROR-MODEL §1: aggregates are NaN on empty input); SymPy's Max() is -oo, the identity element.
julia.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers NaN, Julia raises an error (ArgumentError: reducing over an empty co).
